subject: Re: MAP proposal — witness-test plan & close milestones

Subject: MAP kickoff + initial acceptance checkpoints

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency profiles and the KV caching behavior. Procurement asked us to capture a short mutual action plan so we can align legal/procure milestones to technical validation.

High level asks from our side:
- A short list of acceptance tests we can run during a 4-week pilot (latency, throughput at 99th pct, throughput under batching, and end-to-end inference cost per 1k requests).
- A clear "witness test" step where our infra lead (cc'd) can observe a run and sign-off.
- Any docs we can share with security to accelerate the SOC2 / data handling review.

Can you send a distilled MAP with milestones and who owns each item?

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Kline
Head of Product
CuraTech

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Sarah Kline <sarah@curatech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-28T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + initial acceptance checkpoints

Sarah — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a concise MAP-Proposal-v2.pdf and a witness-test matrix (MAP-Witness-Test-Matrix.xlsx). Key highlights below: 

1) Pilot window: 4 weeks (proposed 2026-07-05 to 2026-07-30)
2) Success criteria (must pass all):
   - 99th percentile latency <= 220ms for production-like queries (seq len ~512)
   - Sustained throughput >= 80 reqs/sec at 75% GPU util for the reserved pool
   - Inference cost per 1k requests <= $X (we'll provide burn estimate once we see sampling)
   - Model output fidelity: >92% on curated evaluation prompts (we'll share the eval set)
3) Witness test: a live 90-minute session where CuraTech infra runs a workload and Redwood co-observes. Sign-off is a simple "witnessed and consistent" note from your infra lead.
4) Exit gate (for moving to contract/paid prod): all criteria above met + security questionnaire (SOC2 evidence) reviewed by CuraTech security.

Next steps: Marissa, can you add the engineering-level acceptance tests (smoke + stress + crash recovery) to the matrix? Lauren/Ben — want me to attach a draft SOW and a proposed purchase timeline for procurement?

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs:
- MAP-Proposal-v2.pdf (pdf)
- MAP-Witness-Test-Matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + initial acceptance checkpoints — engineering tests

Adding the engineering perspective — proposed acceptance tests to be included in the witness-test matrix: 

A) Functional / smoke tests (Day 0):
   - 10 warm-up requests -> verify model loads and KV cache warm-up completes in < 5s
   - Token-level correctness checks on 20 golden prompts (exact match / normalized similarity thresholds)

B) Load/stress (Day 7):
   - Gradual ramp to target throughput (80 reqs/sec) while monitoring 95/99/99.9 pct latencies
   - Memory/KV cache health: no KV cache evictions beyond expected TTL under target workload

C) Fault injection & recovery (Day 14):
   - Simulate node restart during a 15-min sustained load; system must restore to <2x baseline latency within 3 minutes

D) Data controls & logs (continuous):
   - Audit log sample review for 500 random requests (redacted) to verify request/response retention policies

E) Final verification (Day 28):
   - Witness test: run curated eval set (200 prompts) end-to-end, verify >92% fidelity and that latency/throughput targets are satisfied in the same session.

Attachments: I'll drop the witness-test matrix updates to the drive link. For procurement, Lauren: can you propose a two-step PO (pilot, then conversion credit on first year commit)?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Product — Inference | Redwood Inference
